newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt lower in extremely thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt lower in extremely thin trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices were lower across the board in line with U.S. Treasuries but market experts said activity remained extremely thin as local players were absent from the market due to the Easter holiday weekend.

"The backdrop given by Treasuries has not been good and because of the Easter holiday, the market has been light," said a Latin American strategist at a European bank. "There has not been much activity, so everyone is waiting for the beginning of next week to see how the market opens up."
At 1445 EST/1945 GMT, Argentine par bonds were 7/8 lower at 63-1/2 bid, Mexican pars were one percentage point weaker at 71-1/2 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds were 1-3/8 softer at 75 bid.
Even though the Brady market followed the U.S. Treasury market downward, trading sources said yield spreads were pretty much unchanged.
"We are holding in very well in comparison to what is happening with Treasuries. We are basically performing with the bond market," said an emerging market trader at a major U.S. investment bank.

But market experts said the scenario was becoming increasingly more bearish for the emerging debt markets given the precipitous drop in the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond and the growing nervousness about the U.S. interest rate environment.
"With the long (U.S. Treasury) bond at 7.08 percent, our market has nowhere to go but down," said Walter Molano, director of economic and financial research at SBC Warburg.

"We are likely to trade sideways with a downward bias," said the first source, who said that trend is likely to continue until there is a clearer assessment of whether the U.S. Fed funds rate will be raised again and by how much.
At 1400 EST/1900 GMT, the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond closed off 1-8/32, pushing the yield up to 7.09 percent.
Indeed, a further tightening move by the Federal Reserve would paint a far more bearish scenario.
Molano said the great liquidity that fueled crossover buying in the last quarter of 1996 and the first part of 1997 will start to deflate as interest rates trend higher.
"If we have another 100 (basis point tightening) move on the short rates, then the outlook is indeed dire," he added.
Looking ahead to next week, experts said the emerging debt market will be keeping a close watch on key U.S. economic data and the subsequent effects on the U.S. bond market.
The National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) for March is due out Tuesday and the U.S. payrolls report for March is due out Friday.
Elsewhere, trading sources said the strike in Russia against unpaid wages and government policy had little impact on the price of Vnesheconombank loans.
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans were 5/8 lower at 78-5/8 bid and its mark loans were unchanged at 83-5/8.
Among other Eastern European credits, Bulgarian IABs were 1-1/8 weaker at 58-1/8 bid and its FLRBs were 1-1/4 lower at 43-1/4.
